content:
One thing that is currently missing from the draft of the Carleson paper is a declaration about use of AI. In order to prepare this, we need to hear from all contributors about whether you have used AI (either for the Lean code or for paper writing tasks) and, if so, how you have used it specifically.
If you have contributed to the project, please respond in this thread.
Just as an example: I did not use AI in this project, neither for writing Lean code nor for drafting or reviewing the paper.
I did not use AI in this project, neither for writing Lean code nor for drafting or reviewing the paper.

I did not use AI in this project, neither for writing Lean code nor for drafting or reviewing the paper.
(When searching for literature, after a manual search I also asked AI... with very limited results. But I wrote everything by hand.)

I did not use AI in this project for writing Lean code or for drafting the paper. I plan to use AI to review the paper for typos. Btw it may be worth mentioning in the paper, that at the time the main formalization work was completed, AI models (at least publicly available ones, to my knowledge) were not powerful enough to provide meaningful assistance in the formalization. As we know this situation has changed in recent months.
I didn't use AI in this project.

I did not use AI in this project for writing Lean code nor for drafting or reviewing the paper. I have used AI (sparingly) to ask mathematical questions, but the output was not directly copied to any published material.

@channel if you contributed to the project, please respond here (or, if you prefer, DM to me).

Please note that this is not intended to shame anyone, but just so that we can add a use of AI declaration truthfully. This declaration doesn't have to say "we never used AI", and it's fine if certain tasks are AI-assisted (e.g. the ones Joris mentions above).

(Sorry for the ping to the non-contributors)
No I have not used AI in the one PR I did.
I didn't use AI in this project.
I didn’t use AI in this project, in any of my PRs.
I did not use AI in this project.
I did not use AI in this project

I did not use AI while writing Lean code; I did use AI while searching for lemmas (within Mathlib: LeanSearch, within Carleson: "here is a list of all Carleson lemma signatures, find me the one that does xxx")
I also used leansearch. I did not use AI for writing the paper. I explored using Github copilot in the beginning for the formalization but it didn't work and I stopped using it

I used leansearch for finding mathlib lemmas and sometimes other AI tools to search for mathematical results in the literature and online, and to suggest proofs or counterexamples.
I also experimented a few times with using aristotle to fill in sorries (as suggested to me by @Floris van Doorn). I believe the only time I ended up committing something of the output was in https://github.com/ldiedering/carleson/commit/6e9255a32fff16fab30a8ed920fd0c97d0893ee6 which became part of https://github.com/fpvandoorn/carleson/pull/521. I was not really satisfied with the results at the time (a lot of cleanup was needed for some things I could have done myself relatively quickly) and thus stopped any usage when issues with mathlib version requirements arose.
I did not use AI for writing the paper.
Not sure if I count as a contributor, but I did not use "AI"
